parsed.explanation: The operative regime is a latent criminal statute (male same-sex conduct, 5–14 year felonies) that applies to a trans woman read as male, but with no documented enforcement since 2013, no prosecutions of consenting adults, no documented government abuses, no hate-crime record, and the state signing UN SOGI statements in 2011. No trans-specific traveler-facing restriction is documented on any axis: no border screening, custody, facility, or care exposures. The state is a small, thin-data jurisdiction with constitutional protection limited to 'sex', no gender-identity protection, and a 2023 constitutional ban on same-sex marriage — a latent, tangential statute plus open questions (custody classification, document treatment) hold it a step below the acceptance-with-protections tier, but not into the Elevated Risk band, since the worst documented feature is tier 3 (societal disapproval) at most, not state-imposed universal exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented in the record; entry and visa screening for trans visitors is not covered.
entry_documents.protection: State signed UN SOGI joint statements in 2011, signaling no hostile border stance.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor documents are issued by home country; no local gender-marker regime applies.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Penal Code ss.153–155 (felonies, 5–14 years) could theoretically apply to a trans woman read as male; classification at charge/custody is unsourced.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No prosecutions of consenting adults as of 2013; no government abuses reported.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Enforcement data ends 2013; the present is undocumented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No subnational variation; no facility, bathroom or custody-placement rules documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Single statute book, no island-by-island comparison.

care_services.protection: National HIV response includes transgender residents as a key population (2017), showing institutional engagement.
care_services.interaction: No gender-identity protection in law; care access for trans visitors unsourced.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Latent felony statute; heavier penalties than other sexual conduct; 2023 constitutional amendment banned same-sex marriage, signalling conservative direction.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No prosecutions, no government abuses, no documented police targeting.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Traditional customs perpetuate religious/social discrimination per 2013 report.

minors_guardians.exposure: Age of consent asymmetry falls on young men who have sex with men (14% of local men 15–24); no child-specific trans rules documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: No education-policy or youth-service findings in the record.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No hate-crime incidents, statistics or legislation documented; absence in this record is not proof of absence.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin-data jurisdiction; absence of record is not a strong positive signal.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No gender-identity protection anywhere; constitutional protection limited to 'sex'; no partner-visa or foreign-union recognition.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Labour Act 2017 (resident-facing, no GI protection); no visitor-facing remedy documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Statute is latent, not enforced; no recourse tested.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A shows a documented, enforced, universal visitor-facing restriction (border register, routine exclusion). This dossier has no enforced traveler-facing restriction at all — only a latent statute with no prosecutions — so it sits materially above 0.35-A.

0.55-B shows documented secondary screening friction with administrative penalties. This dossier documents no such friction but also no working recourse; its latent statute plus open questions (custody classification, document treatment) place it a step below 0.55-B's documented-but-bounded friction, roughly at the same level or slightly higher.

0.75-C shows trained officers, functioning appeal, and brief detention risk. This dossier lacks documented protective machinery (no recourse, thin data) but also documents less friction and no enforcement; it sits slightly below 0.75-C, around the 0.65 mark.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines a colonial latent felony statute (male same-sex conduct, applicable to a trans woman read as male) with no documented enforcement, no prosecutions since 2013, no government abuses, no hate-crime record, and no trans-specific traveler-facing restriction on any axis. The state signed UN SOGI statements in 2011, and the HIV response includes transgender residents as a key population. Exposures are open questions (custody classification, document treatment, entry screening) rather than documented harms; the 2023 same-sex marriage ban is a resident-facing signal, not traveler exposure. Absence of enforcement data is not proof of safety, but the worst documented feature is latent societal disapproval, not state-imposed universal exposure or targeting. This places the jurisdiction at the boundary between Reduced and Elevated Risk, around 0.65.
